note: Baseline sources for Morning Read, each verified on 2026-11-17 from a cloud container: still publishing, feed tested, an article page read. access: free | partial (some pieces subscriber-only: use free pieces only, skip paywalled ones) | metered. read: page (feed gives links, read the article page) | feed (article pages are blocked; the feed carries the text) | listing (no feed: read the listing page and pick dated items). role: core (scan every run) | creative (rotation: about one piece per edition, read in full, compass mark) | curiosity (Uncategorized finds) | travel (Uncategorized, places) | archive (evergreen, little or no new output: an occasional pick). filter: what to skip in the feed. Category keys match ReadingService.Categories.

sources.name: BBC News – World
sources.why: Neutral baseline of what happened; context for deeper pieces.

sources.name: Al Jazeera English
sources.why: Best free coverage of the Middle East, Africa and South Asia.
sources.caveat: Qatari state funding; Gulf and Israel coverage takes a side.

sources.name: Lowy Institute – The Interpreter
sources.why: Short, sharp analysis of Asia and the Pacific.

sources.name: War on the Rocks
sources.why: Rigorous strategy and military analysis by practitioners.
sources.caveat: US national-security lens; members-only pieces are cut.

sources.name: Carnegie Politika
sources.why: Exiled Russian experts on Russia's economy, elites and foreign policy.

sources.name: International Crisis Group – CrisisWatch
sources.why: Field-based analysis of conflicts nobody else covers; monthly global scan.
sources.caveat: Pages blocked; feed gives short snippets only, so mostly a pointer for open search.

sources.name: Phillips O'Brien
sources.why: Strategic analysis of the Russia–Ukraine war and air power.

sources.name: Daniel Drezner – Drezner's World
sources.why: An IR scholar explaining great-power behaviour clearly.

sources.name: Liberty Street Economics (NY Fed)
sources.why: Short, evidence-led research on banking, labour, inflation and markets.

sources.name: Bank Underground (BoE staff)
sources.why: One central-bank finding per post, with charts and reasoning.

sources.name: ECB Blog
sources.why: Euro-area economics explained by ECB economists.

sources.name: Federal Reserve FEDS Notes
sources.why: Short, rigorous Fed research notes.

sources.name: PIIE Realtime Economics
sources.why: Clear analysis of trade, currencies and global macro.
sources.filter: Feed mixes events; keep blog posts.

sources.name: Timothy Taylor – Conversable Economist
sources.why: Distils research reports on any economic topic into plain English.

sources.name: Joey Politano – Apricitas Economics
sources.why: Data-heavy explainers that teach how to read economic data.

sources.name: Branko Milanovic – Global Inequality and More
sources.why: A leading inequality scholar; distinctive and contrarian.

sources.name: Adam Tooze – Chartbook

sources.name: Carbon Brief
sources.why: Best climate science and policy explainers with original data.

sources.name: Ember
sources.why: Country-level power-sector data on the energy transition.

sources.name: Climate Home News
sources.why: Climate diplomacy and finance with a Global South angle.

sources.name: Energy Institute at Haas
sources.why: Energy economists on prices, fuels and power markets.

sources.name: RealClimate

sources.name: Canary Media

sources.name: Hannah Ritchie – Sustainability by Numbers

sources.name: Zeke Hausfather – The Climate Brink

sources.name: Michael Liebreich

sources.name: IEEE Spectrum

sources.name: Ars Technica – Space

sources.name: Ars Technica – Science

sources.name: Brian Potter – Construction Physics

sources.name: Grady Hillhouse – Practical Engineering

sources.name: Quanta Magazine

sources.name: Nature News

sources.name: Science News
